questions.question_text:
What are the coordinates of $A$? The axes meet at $(0,0)$, and each grid square represents $1$ unit on each axis.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.75]\draw[gray!30,very thin](0,0)grid(6,6);\draw[->](0,0)--(6.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[->](0,0)--(0,6.5)node[above]{$y$};\fill(2,5)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$A$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: The vertical coordinate was written before the horizontal coordinate.
The horizontal coordinate was incorrectly used twice.
The vertical coordinate was incorrectly used twice.

questions.question_text:
What are the coordinates of $B$? The axes meet at $(0,0)$, and each grid square represents $1$ unit on each axis.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.75]\draw[gray!30,very thin](0,0)grid(7,6);\draw[->](0,0)--(7.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[->](0,0)--(0,6.5)node[above]{$y$};\fill(6,3)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$B$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: The coordinates were recorded in vertical-horizontal order.
The horizontal position was used for both coordinates.
The vertical position was used for both coordinates.

questions.solution_text: The horizontal value is $6$ and the vertical value is $3$, so $B=(6,3)$.

questions.question_text:
What are the coordinates of $C$? The axes meet at $(0,0)$, and each grid square represents $1$ unit on each axis.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.75]\draw[gray!30,very thin](0,0)grid(6,6);\draw[->](0,0)--(6.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[->](0,0)--(0,6.5)node[above]{$y$};\fill(0,5)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$C$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: The coordinates were reversed, moving the point to the x-axis.
The zero horizontal position was replaced by the height.
Being on an axis was confused with being at the origin.

questions.solution_text: The point is on the $y$-axis, so $x=0$; its height is $5$.

questions.question_text:
What are the coordinates of $D$? The axes meet at $(0,0)$, and each grid square represents $1$ unit on each axis.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.75]\draw[gray!30,very thin](0,0)grid(6,5);\draw[->](0,0)--(6.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[->](0,0)--(0,5.5)node[above]{$y$};\fill(4,0)circle(2.5pt)node[above]{$D$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: The point's horizontal and vertical positions were reversed.
The baseline was incorrectly read as one instead of zero.
The nonzero horizontal position was ignored.

questions.solution_text: The point is $4$ along the $x$-axis and $0$ up, so $D=(4,0)$.

questions.question_text:
Which plotted point has the same horizontal coordinate as $P$? The axes meet at $(0,0)$, and each grid square represents $1$ unit on each axis.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.75]\draw[gray!30,very thin](0,0)grid(7,7);\draw[->](0,0)--(7.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[->](0,0)--(0,7.5)node[above]{$y$};\fill(3.5,1.5)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$P$};\fill(3.5,5.5)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$Q$};\fill(6.5,1.5)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$R$};\fill(1.5,3.5)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$S$};\fill(5.5,3.5)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$T$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: The same vertical coordinate, $1.5$, was matched instead of the horizontal coordinate.
The coordinates of $P$, $(3.5,1.5)$, were reversed to select $S=(1.5,3.5)$.
The horizontal coordinate of $P$, $3.5$, was matched to the vertical coordinate of $T$.

questions.solution_text: $P=(3.5,1.5)$ and $Q=(3.5,5.5)$ both have horizontal coordinate $3.5$. They lie on the same vertical line.

questions.question_text:
Three vertices of a rectangle are $(1,2)$, $(5,2)$ and $(5,6)$.
Which ordered pair is the fourth vertex?

options.why: The needed horizontal and vertical coordinates were reversed.
The second vertex's coordinates, $(5,2)$, were reversed.
The horizontal coordinate of the upper-right point was used as the height.

questions.solution_text: The missing point shares $x=1$ with the first vertex and $y=6$ with the third, so it is $(1,6)$.
